title: Messages between AI agents, as the Identity Agent that holds them records them (ADR-047)
description: Every message is signed twice. The sender signs a statement (a body, with its machine key) or a request (a person, from a paired controller). The Identity Agent then countersigns a record of it, as the AI agent the message is from, in a signed DIDComm envelope whose body is the record. Worked examples, every byte reproducible from published seeds, are in identity-agent-core/agentmessage/message-vectors.json; contracts/check_ai_agent_vectors.py recomputes them from this prose.

statement_bytes.description: What a body signs: the lines IA-AGENT-MSG-V1 (IA-AGENT-MSG-V2 when the statement has a tier; an empty tier is no tier), conversation, kind, from, to, in_reply_to, body_hash, brain.provider, brain.model, brain.session, brain.run_hash, host, host_nonce, host_time, body_credential, and for V2 only, tier, joined with a newline (0x0a), no trailing newline. An absent field is an empty line, except tier: with no tier the string is V1 with no tier line, exactly as it was before tiers existed, so earlier messages verify unchanged. A reader that does not know tiers rebuilds V1 and so refuses a tiered statement, never runs it without its tier. The signature is made with the body's machine key and encoded as for a signed request (see contracts/agent-body).

statement.description: A body's statement. Refused unless every required field is non-empty, no field holds a carriage return or newline, kind is one of the four, tier if not empty is quick, standard or deep and the kind is ask, in_reply_to is present (a body speaks about a message it was given, so even an ask inside a conversation names the message it was handling; the one exception is an ask that opens a conversation, which names no message and no conversation, and every other statement names its conversation), host_nonce is at least 16 characters and host_time is RFC 3339.

conversation.description: the conversation this is in; empty, and signed as an empty line, only on an ask that acts on no message, which opens a conversation whose identifier the Identity Agent chooses. An opening is admitted only under a grant whose resource constraints state, outright, the AI agents it may open toward (a non-empty list under agent.message.send, key to; a missing one is a refusal, not leave to open toward anyone) and a positive whole number of openings per hour (agent.message.open, key per_hour); the opening's host_nonce is remembered by the Identity Agent so one signed opening opens one conversation (ADR-047, Amendment 3)

in_reply_to.description: the message this one acts on; required by the check although the field may be left out of the JSON, except on an ask that opens a conversation, which acts on none

body_credential.description: the AI Agent Body credential that made host this AI agent's body

tier.description: on an ask only: the tier of model the asker wants the task run on. It is advisory: it names a family, not a model, and the receiving AI agent decides which model it means, from the models its brain allows. A sender adds one only when the receiver is known to read IA-AGENT-MSG-V2 messages (within one organisation's Identity Agent that is always so); otherwise the receiver refuses the ask. An empty tier is absent: the same as none, signed as V1. Absent means the receiver's default. Covered by the signature.

brain.description: What produced the words, as the body reports it. The body's word, not the model provider's.

run_hash.description: a digest of everything the brain was sent and returned in the run

kind.description: An AI agent's kinds are ask, reply, receipt, failure and progress. A person's statement over a fingerprint (ADR-067) is a message, ask, hand-off, split, close or reopen. outcome is the Identity Agent's own note of how a person's entry ended (ADR-068).

party.description: An AI agent's identifier, or person: followed by a person's identifier.

digest.description: Blake3-256 of the words, CESR qb64 with code E.

person_message.description: What a person's controller signs to say something to an AI agent: the words themselves, so the signature covers them.

conversation.description: absent to open a new conversation

controller_proof.description: A person's own statement: the request their controller signed, kept as the exact string signed. Its second line is the controller and its last line the Blake3-256 (CESR) of the request's bytes, which request_bytes carries. The signature is the controller's machine key's, encoded as for a body (see contracts/agent-body). A proof carries exactly one of request_bytes and request.

public_key.description: the controller's key, as its Controller Grant records it

request_bytes.description: The exact bytes of the JSON request the controller signed (a person_message), in standard base64 with padding. The signed string's last line is the Blake3-256 of the decoded bytes. They are carried as a string, not nested as JSON, so a JSON encoder that re-writes the record cannot change them; read the person's words only from these decoded bytes.

request.description: Read only, never written: the request nested as JSON (a person_message), the form records took before request_bytes. The Identity Agent that wrote such a record compacted it and escaped <, > and & as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026 (and U+2028, U+2029 likewise), so a reader takes its bytes as they stand or with exactly those escapes undone, and accepts whichever has the digest the signed string names; neither is accepted otherwise.

controller_grant.description: the controller's Controller Grant credential, when it has one

person_statement.description: When the controller was an app's back end speaking for a person: that person's own signed statement over a fingerprint of their words, as the app carried it. Absent when the controller spoke as the signer it belongs to. The salt of the fingerprint is not here.

person_ref.description: The person a controller acts for, as the Identity Agent established it.

record.description: One entry in a conversation, as the Identity Agent countersigns it. It carries exactly one sender's proof: statement with host_signature and host_verkey, controller_proof, or person_proof; an outcome carries none. A person's entry may instead be a refusal (refusal set), which holds no words. The entry's id is e and its seq, and a person's entry and its outcome are separate entries. What the record says must be what the sender signed. prev_hash is the hash of the entry before it in the conversation (see entry_hash), empty for the first.

to.description: An AI agent's identifier, person: and a person's identifier, a hand-off's or split's new owner as the statement names it, or empty for a close, a reopen and an outcome.

depth.description: how far down a chain of asks: a person's message is 0, and an AI agent's ask that opens a conversation is 1

body_grade.description: the grade of the body it came from, stamped by the Identity Agent

refusal.description: why the Identity Agent refused a person's write before forwarding anything

ciphertext_hash.description: for an entry the Identity Agent holds only as ciphertext: the statement's fingerprint, over the ciphertext

jwm.description: The countersigned message: id is the record's message_id (an entry whose id differs is refused), type is agent-message, from is did:keri: and the countersigner, to is a one-element list of did:keri: and the record's to, with a person: prefix removed, created_time is the record's ia_time, expires_time is empty, and body is the record.

envelope.description: A signed DIDComm envelope (mode signed). plaintext is the base64url (no padding) of the JWM's JSON, its fields in the order id, type, from, to, created_time, expires_time, body. ed_sig and mldsa_sig are base64url signatures by the countersigner's messaging keys over those JSON bytes followed directly by E and the base64url (no padding) of the Blake3-256 of the JWM's body bytes: ed_sig with Ed25519, mldsa_sig with ML-DSA-65 with an empty context, signed deterministically, so both reproduce from the keys. Both must verify. A verifier also accepts signatures over the same JSON bytes followed by the Blake3-256 of the body as a CESR digest (qb64, code E), the form envelopes will be signed over in a later release. The countersigner is the AI agent the message is from, or the Identity Agent itself for a person's message.

entry_hash.description: An entry's place in its conversation's chain: Blake3-256 (CESR qb64, code E) of plaintext, a newline, ed_sig, a newline, mldsa_sig, all as they appear in the envelope.

messaging_keys.description: A countersigner's public messaging keys, base64url without padding. They are tied to the identity by its key log, one of two ways. If its inception's a list holds a seal with ia IA-HYBRID-1, the keys must be the ones it commits to: ka holds [x25519, mlkem768] and, where present, sa holds [ed25519, mldsa65], each as a CESR value under its own type code. Otherwise kel_sig must verify: CESR 0B, an Ed25519 signature by the identity's current key over the ASCII bytes IA-DIDCOMM-KEYS-V1 followed, for each of aid, ed25519, mldsa65, x25519, mlkem768 and cipher_suite in that order, by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian integer and then its bytes.

person_statement.description: What a person's device or session signs: IA-PERSON-MSG-V1 over the fingerprint of their words, never the words (signed-fingerprint.md). Keys are exactly these, in lower case, each at most once, and no value is null: a reader refuses a statement otherwise, as Go's decoder here does.

person_proof.description: A person's own statement for an entry, with no words in it: the statement, the key that signed it and the signature (encoded as for a body, see contracts/agent-body). The record must say what was signed: kind, from (as person: and the statement's from), to, in_reply_to and conversation as the statement has them, and body_hash equal to the statement's fingerprint.

outcome.description: How a pending entry of a person's ended. The chain is append-only, so this is an entry of its own, of kind outcome, from the Identity Agent, with in_reply_to the entry's id and no sender's proof; the countersignature is the proof.

entry.description: the id of the entry, e and its seq

reason.description: required for not-kept, absent for committed
